2.  Warrants

3.  Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report
  State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within 30 days following each
  fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment balances. The purpose
  of the report is to inform, on a quarterly basis, the City’s cash and investment balances,
  the investment types, yields. and market values, and to ensure that the City’s investments
  are in compliance with the City’s adopted investment policy.
  Recommended Action
  Adopt the resolution accepting the FY22-23 Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report.

4.  Annual Sewer Project Request for Proposals
  Annual, City Staff and the City’s Wastewater Treatment Contractor, prioritize specific
  capital improvement projects to upgrade the City’s sewer infrastructure system and
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
AUGUST 1,2023
PAGE 3

  wastewater treatment facility. For Fiscal Year 2023-24, City Staff have identified a scope
  of work to include tour major components.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to solicit a request for proposals for qualified
  firms to implement the City’s Annual Sewer Project Infrastructure Plan (Capital
  Improvement Project Number 205012).

5.  Citywide Street Rehabilitation Program Request for Proposals
  Funded primarily through the monthly highway use tax, the Citywide Street Rehabilitation
  Capital Improvement Project focuses on street pothole repairs and slurry seal throughout
  Avalon, In Fiscal Year 2023-24 there is $350,000 budgeted to facilitate this project.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to solicit a request for proposals for qualified
  firms to implement the City’s Citywide Street Rehabilitation Program (Capital
  Improvement Project Number 180041).

6.  Wastewater Treatment Plant Backup Generator Procurement
  In April 2023 Montrose Engineering, Inc., identified that the backup generator at the City’s
  Wastewater Treatment Plant was non-operable. The generator is essential for operation
  and due for replacement.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the City Manager or his designee to procure a used backup generator in
  accordance with the City’s procurement standards for a not to exceed cost of $85,000.

PUBLIC HEARING

7.  Revised Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Miscellaneous Fee Schedule
  The City charges fees for miscellaneous public services, use of City facilities and
  equipment rental and other activities. User fees are assessed and collected for City
  services and programs provided by various departments. At the June 6, 2023 City Council
  Meeting, Council adopted the FY 23-24 Misc. Fee Schedule; however, upon further
  review, the certain fees required further revisions.
  Recommended Action
  1. Hear a presentation regarding the Miscellaneous Fee Schedule. 2. Open the Public
  Hearing to hear public comments. 3. Close the Public Hearing. 4. If consensus, adopt the
  fee schedule with revisions as proposed.

GENERAL BUSINESS

8.  Moratorium on the Issuance of Transient Rental Licenses for Transient Rental Use to
  New Applicants
  The Avalon Municipal Code (“AMC”) allows for the issuance of a Transient Rental License
  for transient rental uses. The City seeks to balance the desire of property owners to
  supplement their income and provide alternative lodging for visitors against the strain on
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA

  available City housing stock that such transient rental uses place on full-time Avalon
  residents and employees of Avalon businesses.
  Recommended Action
  Approve by four-fifths City Council vote an urgency ordinance of the City of Avalon
  establishing a forty-five day moratorium on the issuance of Transient Rental Licenses
  for transient rental use to new applicants.

SUBJECT:  Fiscal Year 2022-2023 Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt the resolution accepting the FY22-23 Fourth Quarter
Treasurer’s Report.

REPORT SUMMARY: State and Municipal Codes require the Treasurer to submit within
30 days following each fiscal quarter a report summarizing the City’s cash and investment
balances. Attached is the Fourth Quarter Treasurer’s Report for FY22-23. The report was
shared with the City Treasurer prior to presentation to City Council.

The purpose of the report is to inform, on a quarterly basis, the City’s cash and investment
balances, the investment types, yields, and market values, and to ensure that the City’s
investments are in compliance with the City’s adopted investment policy. The report shows that
all of the Citys funds are in compliance with its investment policy. In general, operating cash is
held in US Bank checking accounts and any excess cash is invested in California’s Local
Agency Investment Fund (LAIF) and various certificates of deposit (CDs). In accordance with
Government Code sections 16429.1 and 53601 et seq., the City cannot invest more than 30%
of its portfolio in CDs. CDs accounted for 19.3% of the unrestricted cash and investments for
the quarter ended June 30, 2023.

The unrestricted cash balance for the fourth quarter of 2022-2023 totaled $21.16 million, an
increase of $2.15 million from the third quarter of 2022-2023. The unrestricted cash balance

SUBJECT:  Wastewater Treatment Plant Backup Generator Procurement

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the City Manager or his designee to procure a used
backup generator in accordance with the City’s procurement standards for a not to exceed cost
of $85,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: In April 2023 Montrose Engineering, Inc., identified that the backup
generator at the City’s Wastewater Treatment Plant was non-operable.

After further evaluation, it was determined that the unit had reached the end of its useful life and
it would be inefficient or impossible to facilitate repairs. Staff determined a replacement should
be procured as soon as possible. A dependable primary and backup power source are essential
to the function of the wastewater treatment facility. As a temporary stopgap measure, Staff
located a rental portable generator for the facility to utilize. The cost of the rental is $6300 per
month regardless of whether the generator is in use or not.

Ultimately, the generator is essential for operation and is due for replacement. This expenditure
is identified in the wastewater treatment plant capital improvement plan and budgeted as part of
the City’s annual Major Sewer Projects list for this year under CIP Project #205012.

Due to continued supply chain issues, lead times for new equipment may exceed one year. In
order to facilitate a cost efficient replacement, Staff recommends procurement of a high quality,
used, portable unit. The used generator would serve as an interim replacement at the
wastewater treatment plant until a new permanent generator could be identified and procured.
As soon as a new generator is identified, this item will return to City Council for a formal
procurement request. After a new generator is procured and successfully installed at the
wastewater treatment facility, the used unit may be utilized citywide on a portable basis.

Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager or his designee to procure
a used backup generator in accordance with the City’s procurement standards for a not to
exceed cost of $85,000.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City will continue
to incur monthly rental costs for a backup generator at the wastewater treatment facility while a
permanent solution is identified and implemented.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implementation of City Council direction.

a Transient Rental License (“TRL”) for transient rental uses (AMC § 3-1309). The City seeks
to balance the desire of property owners to supplement their income and provide alternative
lodging for visitors against the strain on available City housing stock that such transient rental
uses place on full-time Avalon residents and employees of Avalon businesses. Previously,
transient rental uses were authorized with a Conditional Use Permit (‘CUP) under AMC §
8404. Following the adoption of a new ordinance, transient rental uses are now authorized
through the issuance of a TRL under the code section above, AMC § 3-1.309. The TRLs do
not run with the land and must be renewed annually.

Currently, the City is addressing all factors that negatively impact long term housing stock, with
an emphasis on affordable housing, and has received complaints from properly owners of the
negative impacts that result from living in close proximity to property that has been granted
either a CUP or TRL for transient rental uses. Specifically, the City has received numerous
complaints in the form of public comment about noise impacts, traffic impacts, and safety
impacts to residents relating to issuance of CUPs and TRLs. A temporary moratorium of the
issuance of TRLs for transient rental uses is immediately necessary to protect existing housing
stock, and to allow City Council, City staff and the City Attorney time to study appropriate
regulations to maintain public safety and health of the community. Additionally, the moratorium
will temporarily halt further issuance of TRLs so that the City can identify regulations which
ensure that issuance of TRLs does not undermine the City’s goals to have affordable housing
stock and maintain a safe community.

The proposed moratorium will disallow the issuance of any TRLs to persons who submit an
application following the effective date of this ordinance. The proposed moratorium will not
prevent those who have already been issued a TRL or CUP from continuing to operate
transient rentals under those entitlements. Applicants who submitted a valid application and
paid the application fee for a TRL before the effective date of this ordinance may still have their
applications heard before the Planning CommissionS There are only three (3) pending
 applications for a TRL at the time of this meeting. Given the low number of pending
applications, and the applicants’ compliance with the City’s existing regulations, Staff
recommends allowing those applications to move forward, since those applicants may have
already incurred costs in preparing for transient rental use.

If the City Council does not approve the urgency ordinance establishing a forty-five day
moratorium on the issuance of TRLs for transient rental use by a four-fifths vote, and non-
urgency ordinance may be adopted after two readings and such ordinance would go into effect
30 days after adoption. If no moratorium is passed, TRLs will continued to be process under
existing regulations until such regulations are changed.

FISCAL IMPACTS: None.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION:  The Citys existing
rules for the granting of transient occupancy licenses will remain in place.
